Hi [PERSON_NAME_8008] and Singular team,
We have unfortunate news. Harmony Games Inc. is shutting down and preparing to file for dissolution.
Because of this, we need to terminate our agreement with Singular effective immediately. Unfortunately, the company is insolvent and we have no cash reserves left, There are no funds available to pay any remaining balance.
We have valued the relationship and the team at Singular. We have not come close to using the plan, we have spent well under 1% of our ad spend cap, and we would appreciate your help in making this a clean, mutual early termination so we can properly close down without leaving obligations on your books.
Please confirm in writing that the contract and any related renewals are cancelled as of today, and let us know what you need from us to close the account and stop any further charges. If helpful, we can provide the stamp-certified Certificate of Dissolution once filed to support your internal closeout.
Thank you,
 Leonard Hayes", "channel": "C0ADGSZKR3R", "user": "EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID"}, {"ts": "1770932147.282819", "type": "message", "text": "<@EMPLOYEE_0025_SLACK_ID> note for Unity team

Hi Unity Team,
We have unfortunate news. Our company, Harmony Games is shutting down and preparing to file for dissolution.

Because of this, we are terminating our Unity Pro licensing agreement effective immediately. Unfortunately, the company is insolvent and we have no cash reserves left, There are no funds available to pay any remaining balance. We are filing for the Certificate of Dissolution once we resolve this one last item, as we’re working with existing vendors to properly shut down without any obligations on their books.

Please confirm in writing that the contract and any related renewals are cancelled as of today, and let us know what you need from us to close the account and stop any further charges. If helpful, we can provide the stamp-certified Certificate of Dissolution once filed to support your internal closeout.

Thank you,

This is a key distinction from binary files like documents or videos that users upload. However, other file size limits apply to media that a Mini App or bot might send or receive.\\n\\nFile size restrictions for Telegram bots and Mini Apps\\nStandard Bot API\\nIf your game uses the standard Telegram Bot API to send files (e.g., images, videos, or game assets), the following file size limits apply:\\n\\n\\u2022 *Photos:* 10 MB maximum.\\n\\u2022 *Other files (including game assets):* 50 MB maximum. \\n\\u2022 \\nLocal Bot API server\\nFor developers who need to exceed the standard limits, Telegram allows running a local Bot API server. This method significantly increases the file size limit:\\n\\n\\u2022 *Upload limit:* 2000 MB (2 GB) per file.\\n\\u2022 *Total payload limit:* 4000 MB (4 GB) for requests involving multiple files, like a media group.\\n\\u2022 *Premium user uploads:* A local Bot API server supports file sizes larger than 2000 MB, but only if the user uploading them has a Telegram Premium subscription. This is a key distinction from binary files like documents or videos that users upload. However, other file size limits apply to media that a Mini App or bot might send or receive.\\n\\nFile size restrictions for Telegram bots and Mini Apps\\nStandard Bot API\\nIf your game uses the standard Telegram Bot API to send files (e.g., images, videos, or game assets), the following file size limits apply:\\n\\n\\u2022 *Photos:* 10 MB maximum.\\n\\u2022 *Other files (including game assets):* 50 MB maximum. \\n\\u2022 \\nLocal Bot API server\\nFor developers who need to exceed the standard limits, Telegram allows running a local Bot API server. This method significantly increases the file size limit:\\n\\n\\u2022 *Upload limit:* 2000 MB (2 GB) per file.\\n\\u2022 *Total payload limit:* 4000 MB (4 GB) for requests involving multiple files, like a media group.\\n\\u2022 *Premium user uploads:* A local Bot API server supports file sizes larger than 2000 MB, but only if the user uploading them has a Telegram Premium subscription. • Initial term: 12 months is fine, but we would like to add mutual termination for convenience after an initial test period. For example: after the first 3 months from launch, either party can terminate for convenience on 30 days written notice.

*3- Transferability and assignment*
We are not comfortable with a fully transferable license that can be assigned freely.
• The license should be non-transferable except to your wholly owned affiliates.
• Any assignment or transfer to a third party should require our prior written consent.
*4- Monetization and outbound links*
We understand that you control monetization on your portals, but we would appreciate some room to promote our own ecosystem. Is it possible to include links to the iOS and Android store pages for Domino Delights and Zombie Match 3D? These links can follow your UX guidelines. *5- SDK and post termination support*
We are fine integrating your SDK and keeping it up to date during the term, but not for an extended period after termination.
• Please remove the requirement to update or re-integrate the SDK for up to one year after termination.We are happy to commit to updating the SDK during the transition period.
• Post termination, we are happy to commit to keeping the last live version stable for a short transition period (for example 60 days), with critical bug fixes only and no new features or SDK migrations.
If you can accommodate these changes, we will be in a good position to move ahead quickly. Feel free to send a revised draft, or if it is easier, we can mark up the current one and return a redline.
Best regards,

Telegram games, which are built as Mini Apps, do not have a binary size restriction because they are web applications hosted on a developer’s server, not static files uploaded to Telegram’s servers. This is a key distinction from binary files like documents or videos that users upload. However, other file size limits apply to media that a Mini App or bot might send or receive.

File size restrictions for Telegram bots and Mini Apps
Standard Bot API
If your game uses the standard Telegram Bot API to send files (e.g., images, videos, or game assets), the following file size limits apply:

• *Photos:* 10 MB maximum.
• *Other files (including game assets):* 50 MB maximum. 
• 
Local Bot API server
For developers who need to exceed the standard limits, Telegram allows running a local Bot API server. This method significantly increases the file size limit:

• *Upload limit:* 2000 MB (2 GB) per file.
• *Total payload limit:* 4000 MB (4 GB) for requests involving multiple files, like a media group.
• *Premium user uploads:* A local Bot API server supports file sizes larger than 2000 MB, but only if the user uploading them has a Telegram Premium subscription. Bots themselves cannot have a Premium account an[USERNAME_1352] therefore cannot upload files larger than 2000 MB. 
• 
Development and performance considerations
Game logic and assets
Since Mini Apps are web-based, the total size of your game is only limited by your hosting environment and browser performance. The following strategies are recommended for optimizing performance:

• *Server-side optimization:* Keep your game logic on your own server to minimize the data sent to the user.
• *Asset compression:* Compress and optimize images, videos, and other assets to reduce loading times. Tools like TinyPNG can help significantly.
• *Lazy loading:* Only load assets when they are needed, rather than all at once, to improve the initial loading speed.

Definitions
• Revenue: cash collected from Telegram users attributable to [PERSON_NAME_0133].
• Direct costs: UA on Telegram, creator payouts, refunds, chargebacks, payment processing, platform fees, promo credits, other variable costs.
• Net Profit: Revenue minus Direct costs, calculated monthly.
Tiered profit share, per month
• 20% on the first $25,000 of Net Profit
• 15% on the next $50,000 of Net Profit, i.e., $25,001 to $75,000
• 10% on Net Profit above $75,000
• Monthly cap: total payout to [PERSON_NAME_0133] cannot exceed $15,000 for that month
• Floor: if Net Profit is positive but under $5,000, pay the greater of calculated share or $500
• No payout if Net Profit ≤ 0
Why this structure
• Starts aggressive on the first dollars of profit, then steps down to 10%.
• The cap is reached at $100,000 monthly Net Profit:
    ◦ 20% of first $25,000 = $5,000
    ◦ 15% of next $50,000 = $7,500, cumulative $12,500
    ◦ 10% of next $25,000 = $2,500, cumulative $15,000 cap
Examples
1. Your scenario
• Revenue: 100,000 users × $0.50 = $50,000
• Direct costs: $10,000
• Net Profit: $40,000
• Payout: 20% of $25,000 = $5,000, plus 15% of $15,000 = $2,250, total $7,250
2. Strong month
• Net Profit: $100,000
• Uncapped math would be $16,250, but the monthly cap applies, payout = $15,000
3. Modest month
• Net Profit: $4,000
• Calculated share at 20% = $800, floor applies only if higher than share. Payout = $800
Attribution and scope
• Scope: Telegram only, assets [PERSON_NAME_0133] manages.
• Attribution: unique links or postbacks. Mixed traffic allocated by last touch on Telegram assets [PERSON_NAME_0133] controls.
• Refunds and chargebacks reduce Revenue in the period recognized.
Payment terms
• Close books on the 5th, pay by the 15th.
• Monthly report: Users, Revenue, Direct costs, Net Profit, tier math, and payout.

What the contract actually does (plain summary)\\n*Parties and scope*\\n\\u2022 Between MAXFLOW BV (CrazyGames) as Publisher and Harmony Games as Partner.\\n\\u2022 Covers Domino Delights and Zombie Match 3D.\\n\\u2022 License: world-wide, non-exclusive, _transferable_ license to publish the games on \\u201cLicensed Platforms.\\u201d\\n*Licensed Platforms*\\nDefined very broadly as:\\n\\u2022 <http://CrazyGames.com|CrazyGames.com> and its domains / apps\\n\\u2022 other WebGL or HTML5 browser platforms\\n\\u2022 mobile app stores\\nSo by default this contract covers both web and mobile, not just CrazyGames.\\n*Revenue share*\\n\\u2022 Game Revenue is defined as ad + IAP revenue _after_ deducting: agency commissions, ad serving costs, platform fees, payment processing, and VAT/other taxes.\\n\\u2022 Net amount is then split: 40 % Publisher, 60 % Partner.\\n*Hosting and SDK*\\n\\u2022 Technology is \\u201cPublisher hosting\\u201d for these games, so you give them a full build, they host it.\\n\\u2022 You must integrate their SDK, keep it up to date, and, on request, update SDK to the most recent version up to 1 year _after termination_ or make it possible for them to integrate the SDK into the game themselves.\\n*Game updates and parity*\\nYou must:\\n\\u2022 Deliver the game within 6 months.\\n\\u2022 Keep the web version \\u201calways identical to the latest version\\u201d on your own sites and any other platforms.\\n\\u2022 Ship updates to them no later than anyone else, fix bugs promptly, and provide reasonable ongoing support.\\n*Outbound links and monetization*\\n\\u2022 You cannot include outbound links in the game (for example to your site or app stores) without their explicit written consent.\\n\\u2022 They have the exclusive right to serve ads and IAPs on Licensed Platforms. You can only include IAPs with their approval.\\n*Term, renewal, and transition*\\n\\u2022 Initial term: 1 year starting when the game is released on the Licensed Platforms.\\n\\u2022 Automatic renewal for the same period, unless a party gives 3 months written notice before the end of a term.\\n\\u2022 After expiry or termination, they _may_ keep the game live for a 6-month \\u201cTransition Period\\u201d and you must keep providing services and cooperation during that time.\\n*Termination*\\n\\u2022 Both parties can terminate for material breach, insolvency, etc., with cure periods for some items.\\n\\u2022 Publisher has extra rights to terminate immediately, without liability, if There is alleged IP infringement, breach of warranties, or breach of your obligations.\\n\\u2022 There is _no_ mutual termination for convenience anywhere.\\n*Liability, indemnity, and IP*\\n\\u2022 You give broad warranties that you own all IP, do not infringe, comply with laws, no viruses, high quality, etc.\\n\\u2022 You indemnify them for IP infringements, legal breaches, and any claims about game content, with no explicit cap.\\n\\u2022 Their liability is capped at \\u201cfees paid or payable to Partner under the Agreement\\u201d and they disclaim most warranties for their portal.\\n\\u2022 They can act in your name to issue takedowns against copycats, but have no duty to litigate.\\n*Data and marketing*\\n\\u2022 Each party is an independent controller for personal data, must comply with GDPR etc.\\n\\u2022 You cannot use personal data beyond what is necessary, and cannot promote your own or third-party content on their platforms without their written consent.\\n*Law and venue*\\n\\u2022 Governing law: Belgium.\\n\\u2022 Exclusive courts: Leuven, Belgium.\\n2. Key red flags and items to Push on\\nA. Platform scope: they are grabbing mobile by default\\nProblem:\\n\\u2022 Licensed Platforms includes \\u201cmobile app stores,\\u201d and the license is world-wide, transferable, and covers publishing and monetization There.\\n\\u2022 Combined with their exclusive right to serve ads and IAP on Licensed Platforms, this pulls mobile into their control unless you carve it out.\\nPushback / clarification:\\n\\u2022 Restrict the Licensed Platforms to _web only_ for this agreement, for example:\\n    \\u25e6 \\u201cLicensed Platforms: <http://www.CrazyGames.com|www.CrazyGames.com> and other HTML5/WebGL browser game portals. For the avoidance of doubt, this Agreement does not apply to any mobile app store distribution.\\u201d\\n\\u2022 Or, if you want to allow some mobile experiment later, create a _separate_ mobile addendum with tight scope and your veto on any mobile publishing.\\nThis aligns with your plan to keep mobile separate and talk to other mobile publishers.\\n\\nB. Transferable license + easy assignment by them\\nProblem:\\n\\u2022 License is explicitly \\u201ctransferable.\\u201d\\n\\u2022 Assignment clause lets _them_ assign the whole agreement to a third party with only notification, while you cannot assign without their consent.\\nThis means they can sell or spin out your games\\u2019 web rights to another company without your approval.\\nPushback:\\n\\u2022 Make the license non-transferable except to their owned affiliates, or require your prior written consent for any assignment or sublicensing to non-affiliates.\\n\\u2022 Make assignment more symmetric: you can at least assign to an acquirer of Harmony Games without needing their consent.\\nC. Term, auto-renewal, no convenience exit, plus 6-month transition\\nProblem:\\n\\u2022 Initial 1-year term, automatic 1-year renewals, and you must give 3 months notice before the term ends to stop renewal.\\n\\u2022 After any end, they can keep the game live for 6 more months, and you must support it.\\n\\u2022 There is no termination for convenience for you at all.\\nIn practice that is a long lockdown. If you miss the 3-month window, you are locked for another year plus up to 6 months of transition.\\nPushback:\\n\\u2022 Add mutual termination for convenience, for example:\\n    \\u25e6 \\u201cAfter the first 3 months from launch, either Party may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon 30 days written notice.\\u201d\\n\\u2022 Reduce the Transition Period or remove it. If you accept any transition, limit it to 30 days, and clarify that:\\n    \\u25e6 Your support obligation is minimal (no new features, only critical bug fixes).\\n    \\u25e6 They cannot launch the game on new platforms during the transition.\\n\\u2022 If they insist on the 6-month Transition Period, tie it only to expiry of a term, not to early termination for convenience or breach.\\nThis directly reduces the lockdown period you are worried about.\\n\\nD. SDK and support obligations, including after termination\\nProblem:\\n\\u2022 You must implement and keep their SDK up to date, and on request update it \\u201cuntil 1 year after termination,\\u201d or else \\u201cmake it possible for Publisher to integrate the SDK within the Game(s) itself.\\u201d\\n\\u2022 You must keep the web version identical to the latest version on all other platforms, deliver updates to them no later than others, quickly fix defects, and answer their questions.\\nRisks:\\n\\u2022 You are on the hook for live-ops style support even when the deal is effectively over.\\n\\u2022 \\u201cMake it possible for Publisher to integrate the SDK\\u201d is vague and could be interpreted as pressure to expose more of your build pipeline or code than you want.\\nPushback:\\n\\u2022 Limit post-termination obligations: for example, \\u201cup to 60 days after termination, best-effort support limited to critical bug fixes, no new SDK integrations.\\u201d\\n\\u2022 Clarify that you are not required to provide source code or build scripts and that SDK integration will always be done by you at your discretion.\\n\\u2022 Relax \\u201calways identical\\u201d wording so you can test features on other platforms first or maintain a lighter web build.\\nE. Monetization and outbound links: they control everything\\nProblem:\\n\\u2022 They have the exclusive right to serve ads and IAPs within the game on Licensed Platforms.\\n\\u2022 You cannot add Outbound Links or promote your own or third-party content through their platforms without explicit written consent.\\nImpact:\\n\\u2022 You cannot naturally promote your own mobile versions or cross-promote your other games from the web build without their explicit permission.\\n\\u2022 Any IAP system in the web version requires their approval and flows through their billing.\\nPushback:\\n\\u2022 Carve out specific outbound links that are always allowed, for example:\\n    \\u25e6 \\u201cPartner may include links to Partner\\u2019s official website, and to Domino Delights and Zombie Match mobile store pages, subject to Publisher\\u2019s UX requirements, without separate written approval.\\u201d\\n\\u2022 Clarify that cross-promotion of your own titles within the game is permitted, provided it does not conflict with their ad inventory.\\n\\u2022 If you ever want to test your own IAP stack on web, you need at least a negotiation clause instead of pure veto.\\nF. Indemnities and liability are very one-sided\\nProblem:\\n\\u2022 Your indemnity is broad and uncapped in the text: IP infringement, data protection, any claims about content, plus breach of warranties.\\n\\u2022 Their total liability is capped at \\u201cthe fees paid or payable to Partner,\\u201d and they generally disclaim warranties for their site.\\nThis means:\\n\\u2022 Worst-case legal risks related to content, data, or IP are largely on you, while their downside is effectively limited to what they have already paid you.\\nPushback:\\n\\u2022 Add a reciprocal indemnity from them covering:\\n    \\u25e6 Their SDK, ad tech, tracking, and any UA / ad network practices on their side.\\n    \\u25e6 Infringement by their branding or assets, and violations of data protection laws arising from their processing.\\n\\u2022 Introduce caps and carve-outs:\\n    \\u25e6 Cap your indemnity and their liability at a defined multiple of annual fees, with higher caps only for IP or data breaches if needed.\\n\\u2022 Tighten the IP warranties so you are not giving absolute guarantees far beyond what is realistic.\\nG. Right of first refusal on variations (sequels etc.)\\nProblem:\\n\\u2022 The exclusivity clause says that where There is an exclusive game, Publisher has a right of first refusal on variations (sequels, prequels, etc.) under the same terms and conditions.\\nIn this specific Game Order the license is \\u201cnon-exclusive,\\u201d so this clause should not bite now, but it is still sitting There.\\nPushback:\\n\\u2022 Explicitly state in the main agreement or Game Order that:\\n    \\u25e6 \\u201cThe exclusivity provisions and right of first refusal in Annex 2, Article 8 do not apply to this Agreement or to any variations of the Games unless explicitly agreed in a future Game Order.\\u201d\\nThis prevents later arguments that you owe them first dibs on sequels.\\n\\nH. Self-billing, reporting, and audit\\nProblem:\\n\\u2022 They issue self-billing invoices and if you do not object within a short time window, they are deemed accepted.\\n\\u2022 Strong offset rights if ad networks fail to pay them.\\n\\u2022 No explicit reporting detail or audit rights are spelled out.\\nPushback:\\n\\u2022 Ask for:\\n    \\u25e6 Monthly detailed revenue reports by platform, geography, ad network, and ad/IAP split.\\n    \\u25e6 A clear dispute window of at least 30 days from receipt of a statement, with a defined process.\\n    \\u25e6 A right to audit or have a third-party auditor review their numbers once per year at your cost if discrepancies above a threshold are found.\\nI. Governing law and venue\\nProblem:\\n\\u2022 Belgium law, courts of Leuven for any disputes.\\nIf you can live with that, you leave it. If you want less friction:\\n\\u2022 Propose arbitration in a neutral venue or at least a less one-sided forum clause.\\n\\u2022 At minimum, you can leave this as \\u201cnot a hill to die on\\u201d if your main concern is web scope and lock-in, but be aware of the litigation friction.\\n3. Priority list given your goals\\nGiven what you said you care about (web only, shorter lockdown, easy exit, control if they disappoint), I would prioritize:\\n1. *Scope and platforms*: Remove \\u201cmobile app stores\\u201d from Licensed Platforms and make this a pure web publishing deal.\\n2. *Term and exit*: Add mutual termination for convenience with 30 days notice after an initial test period, and shorten or heavily constrain the 6-month Transition Period.\\n3. *Transferability / assignment*: Remove transferability beyond affiliates and require your consent for assignments.\\n4. *Monetization and links*: Explicit rights to link to and promote your own mobile versions and titles, within clear UX bounds.\\n5. *Indemnity balance*: Add mutual SDK / UA indemnity, cap your exposure, and fix the asymmetry.\\n6. *Support tail*: Limit SDK and support obligations after termination.\\nIf you paste your current redline or the email you are sending back, I can rewrite it to focus precisely on these points so There is no ambiguity.\", \"channel\": \"C07C2866011\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID\", \"thread_ts\": \"1763421013.739279\"}, {\"ts\": \"1764793154.009679\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"Short answer: for a venture-backed US studio like Harmony Games, you should assume *somewhere in the 20k\\u201380k USD range for legal + related professional fees*, with a realistic \\u201cplan for pain\\u201d budget around *50k*. I will break down why and how to Push it to the low end.\\nI am not your lawyer or accountant, so treat this as planning guidance and sanity check, not formal advice.\\n\\n1. What drives the cost\\nKey factors that matter for Harmony Games specifically:\\n1. *Type of company and complexity*\\n    \\u25e6 Delaware C-corp with investors and a real cap table.\\n    \\u25e6 Multiple SAFEs / equity holders.\\n    \\u25e6 Employment / contractor agreements across countries.\\n    \\u25e6 Multiple commercial contracts (publishers, ad networks, platforms, vendors).\\n2. More complexity pushes you away from \\u201csimple startup dissolution\\u201d pricing and into custom work.\\n3. *Where fees show up*\\n4.  You are not just paying for \\u201cfile a dissolution form\\u201d:\\n    \\u25e6 corporate / securities law work.\\n    \\u25e6 Contract review and termination.\\n    \\u25e6 Employment and IP issues.\\n    \\u25e6 Tax and accounting cleanup.\\n    \\u25e6 Possibly some board / investor process work (consents, releases, etc.).\\n5. *Your goal*\\n    \\u25e6 If you want a \\u201cclean, defendable shutdown\\u201d that future investors and acquirers will not side-eye, you will spend more than the absolute bare minimum.\\n    \\u25e6 If you are ok with more \\u201cduct tape,\\u201d you can cut costs, but you increase risk of something biting you later.\\n2. Rough fee ranges by category\\nThese are order-of-magnitude numbers for a company like yours, using a mix of decent startup counsel + a scrappy accountant, not BigLaw overkill.\\nA. corporate dissolution & governance: *10k\\u201330k*\\nCovers things like:\\n\\u2022 Board and stockholder approvals.\\n\\u2022 Formal dissolution with Delaware, plus any foreign registrations (e.g. NC, CA, WA).\\n\\u2022 Handling investor rights, preference stack, and confirming There is no distribution or a small pro-rata distribution.\\n\\u2022 Drafting or reviewing:\\n    \\u25e6 Plan of liquidation / dissolution.\\n    \\u25e6 Officer certificates.\\n    \\u25e6 Releases and indemnities where needed.\\nIf everything is organized and you work with current counsel efficiently, you might land around *10k\\u201315k*. If lots of custom questions, messy history, or negotiations, *20k\\u201330k*.\\nB. Contracts, IP, and \\u201cshutting the business off\\u201d: *5k\\u201320k*\\nIncludes:\\n\\u2022 Reviewing and terminating:\\n    \\u25e6 publishing deals (Boombit, CrazyGames, etc.).\\n    \\u25e6 Platform agreements ([ORG_NAME_0308], IronSource, ad networks).\\n    \\u25e6 Vendor and contractor agreements.\\n\\u2022 Cleaning up IP:\\n    \\u25e6 Making sure all game code and assets are properly assigned to the company, so There is no surprise claim later.\\n    \\u25e6 Deciding what happens to IP: kept in the entity that will be dissolved, sold, or assigned to founders or a new entity.\\n\\u2022 Dealing with licenses (engine, SDKs) and privacy / data issues.\\nIf you have reasonably standard contracts and you are willing to send most termination notices yourself, lawyer time can be *5k\\u201310k*. they may assign to a third party on notice.\\nAssessment\\n\\u2022 They added a \\u201cconsent\\u201d qualifier to the license line, which is a small improvement, but:\\n    \\u25e6 It does not explicitly say it is _your_ consent.\\n    \\u25e6 The underlying assignment clause still gives them very broad freedom to assign the agreement and leaves you restricted.\\n\\u2022 This is not fully addressed.\\n4) Monetization and outbound links\\nYour ask\\n\\u2022 They keep ad rights on their portals, but you get guaranteed rights to:\\n    \\u25e6 link to your website.\\n    \\u25e6 link to iOS/Android store pages for Domino Delights and Zombie Match.\\n    \\u25e6 Cross-promote your own titles as long as it does not conflict with their ad placements.\\nWhat they did\\n\\u2022 Outbound Links clause still bans any external links without explicit written consent.\\n\\u2022 Monetization clause still gives them exclusive control of in-game ads and IAP on Licensed Platforms and requires their approval for IAPs.\\nAssessment\\n\\u2022 Not addressed at all.\\n\\u2022 You still cannot even guarantee a \\u201cGet it on iOS/Android\\u201d button without their ad hoc approval.\\n5) Indemnities and liability\\nYour ask\\n\\u2022 Reciprocal indemnity for their SDK, ad tech, and data processing.\\n\\u2022 Reasonable mutual liability caps, not just one-sided.\\nWhat they did\\n\\u2022 Warranty and indemnity framework is unchanged. What the contract actually does (plain summary)\\n*Parties and scope*\\n\\u2022 Between MAXFLOW BV (CrazyGames) as Publisher and Harmony Games as Partner.\\n\\u2022 Covers Domino Delights and Zombie Match 3D.\\n\\u2022 License: world-wide, non-exclusive, _transferable_ license to publish the games on \\u201cLicensed Platforms.\\u201d\\n*Licensed Platforms*\\nDefined very broadly as:\\n\\u2022 <http://CrazyGames.com|CrazyGames.com> and its domains / apps\\n\\u2022 other WebGL or HTML5 browser platforms\\n\\u2022 mobile app stores\\nSo by default this contract covers both web and mobile, not just CrazyGames.\\n*Revenue share*\\n\\u2022 Game Revenue is defined as ad + IAP revenue _after_ deducting: agency commissions, ad serving costs, platform fees, payment processing, and VAT/other taxes.\\n\\u2022 Net amount is then split: 40 % Publisher, 60 % Partner.\\n*Hosting and SDK*\\n\\u2022 Technology is \\u201cPublisher hosting\\u201d for these games, so you give them a full build, they host it.\\n\\u2022 You must integrate their SDK, keep it up to date, and, on request, update SDK to the most recent version up to 1 year _after termination_ or make it possible for them to integrate the SDK into the game themselves.\\n*Game updates and parity*\\nYou must:\\n\\u2022 Deliver the game within 6 months.\\n\\u2022 Keep the web version \\u201calways identical to the latest version\\u201d on your own sites and any other platforms.\\n\\u2022 Ship updates to them no later than anyone else, fix bugs promptly, and provide reasonable ongoing support.\\n*Outbound links and monetization*\\n\\u2022 You cannot include outbound links in the game (for example to your site or app stores) without their explicit written consent.\\n\\u2022 They have the exclusive right to serve ads and IAPs on Licensed Platforms. You can only include IAPs with their approval.\\n*Term, renewal, and transition*\\n\\u2022 Initial term: 1 year starting when the game is released on the Licensed Platforms.\\n\\u2022 Automatic renewal for the same period, unless a party gives 3 months written notice before the end of a term.\\n\\u2022 After expiry or termination, they _may_ keep the game live for a 6-month \\u201cTransition Period\\u201d and you must keep providing services and cooperation during that time.\\n*Termination*\\n\\u2022 Both parties can terminate for material breach, insolvency, etc., with cure periods for some items.\\n\\u2022 Publisher has extra rights to terminate immediately, without liability, if There is alleged IP infringement, breach of warranties, or breach of your obligations.\\n\\u2022 There is _no_ mutual termination for convenience anywhere.\\n*Liability, indemnity, and IP*\\n\\u2022 You give broad warranties that you own all IP, do not infringe, comply with laws, no viruses, high quality, etc.\\n\\u2022 You indemnify them for IP infringements, legal breaches, and any claims about game content, with no explicit cap.\\n\\u2022 Their liability is capped at \\u201cfees paid or payable to Partner under the Agreement\\u201d and they disclaim most warranties for their portal.\\n\\u2022 They can act in your name to issue takedowns against copycats, but have no duty to litigate.\\n*Data and marketing*\\n\\u2022 Each party is an independent controller for personal data, must comply with GDPR etc.\\n\\u2022 You cannot use personal data beyond what is necessary, and cannot promote your own or third-party content on their platforms without their written consent.\\n*Law and venue*\\n\\u2022 Governing law: Belgium.\\n\\u2022 Exclusive courts: Leuven, Belgium.\\n2. Key red flags and items to Push on\\nA. Platform scope: they are grabbing mobile by default\\nProblem:\\n\\u2022 Licensed Platforms includes \\u201cmobile app stores,\\u201d and the license is world-wide, transferable, and covers publishing and monetization There.\\n\\u2022 Combined with their exclusive right to serve ads and IAP on Licensed Platforms, this pulls mobile into their control unless you carve it out.\\nPushback / clarification:\\n\\u2022 Restrict the Licensed Platforms to _web only_ for this agreement, for example:\\n    \\u25e6 \\u201cLicensed Platforms: <http://www.CrazyGames.com|www.CrazyGames.com> and other HTML5/WebGL browser game portals. For the avoidance of doubt, this Agreement does not apply to any mobile app store distribution.\\u201d\\n\\u2022 Or, if you want to allow some mobile experiment later, create a _separate_ mobile addendum with tight scope and your veto on any mobile publishing.\\nThis aligns with your plan to keep mobile separate and talk to other mobile publishers.\\n\\nB. Transferable license + easy assignment by them\\nProblem:\\n\\u2022 License is explicitly \\u201ctransferable.\\u201d\\n\\u2022 Assignment clause lets _them_ assign the whole agreement to a third party with only notification, while you cannot assign without their consent.\\nThis means they can sell or spin out your games\\u2019 web rights to another company without your approval.\\nPushback:\\n\\u2022 Make the license non-transferable except to their owned affiliates, or require your prior written consent for any assignment or sublicensing to non-affiliates.\\n\\u2022 Make assignment more symmetric: you can at least assign to an acquirer of Harmony Games without needing their consent.\\nC. Term, auto-renewal, no convenience exit, plus 6-month transition\\nProblem:\\n\\u2022 Initial 1-year term, automatic 1-year renewals, and you must give 3 months notice before the term ends to stop renewal.\\n\\u2022 After any end, they can keep the game live for 6 more months, and you must support it.\\n\\u2022 There is no termination for convenience for you at all.\\nIn practice that is a long lockdown. If you miss the 3-month window, you are locked for another year plus up to 6 months of transition.\\nPushback:\\n\\u2022 Add mutual termination for convenience, for example:\\n    \\u25e6 \\u201cAfter the first 3 months from launch, either Party may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon 30 days written notice.\\u201d\\n\\u2022 Reduce the Transition Period or remove it. If you accept any transition, limit it to 30 days, and clarify that:\\n    \\u25e6 Your support obligation is minimal (no new features, only critical bug fixes).\\n    \\u25e6 They cannot launch the game on new platforms during the transition.\\n\\u2022 If they insist on the 6-month Transition Period, tie it only to expiry of a term, not to early termination for convenience or breach.\\nThis directly reduces the lockdown period you are worried about.\\n\\nD. SDK and support obligations, including after termination\\nProblem:\\n\\u2022 You must implement and keep their SDK up to date, and on request update it \\u201cuntil 1 year after termination,\\u201d or else \\u201cmake it possible for Publisher to integrate the SDK within the Game(s) itself.\\u201d\\n\\u2022 You must keep the web version identical to the latest version on all other platforms, deliver updates to them no later than others, quickly fix defects, and answer their questions.\\nRisks:\\n\\u2022 You are on the hook for live-ops style support even when the deal is effectively over.\\n\\u2022 \\u201cMake it possible for Publisher to integrate the SDK\\u201d is vague and could be interpreted as pressure to expose more of your build pipeline or code than you want.\\nPushback:\\n\\u2022 Limit post-termination obligations: for example, \\u201cup to 60 days after termination, best-effort support limited to critical bug fixes, no new SDK integrations.\\u201d\\n\\u2022 Clarify that you are not required to provide source code or build scripts and that SDK integration will always be done by you at your discretion.\\n\\u2022 Relax \\u201calways identical\\u201d wording so you can test features on other platforms first or maintain a lighter web build.\\nE. Monetization and outbound links: they control everything\\nProblem:\\n\\u2022 They have the exclusive right to serve ads and IAPs within the game on Licensed Platforms.\\n\\u2022 You cannot add Outbound Links or promote your own or third-party content through their platforms without explicit written consent.\\nImpact:\\n\\u2022 You cannot naturally promote your own mobile versions or cross-promote your other games from the web build without their explicit permission.\\n\\u2022 Any IAP system in the web version requires their approval and flows through their billing.\\nPushback:\\n\\u2022 Carve out specific outbound links that are always allowed, for example:\\n    \\u25e6 \\u201cPartner may include links to Partner\\u2019s official website, and to Domino Delights and Zombie Match mobile store pages, subject to Publisher\\u2019s UX requirements, without separate written approval.\\u201d\\n\\u2022 Clarify that cross-promotion of your own titles within the game is permitted, provided it does not conflict with their ad inventory.\\n\\u2022 If you ever want to test your own IAP stack on web, you need at least a negotiation clause instead of pure veto.\\nF. Indemnities and liability are very one-sided\\nProblem:\\n\\u2022 Your indemnity is broad and uncapped in the text: IP infringement, data protection, any claims about content, plus breach of warranties.\\n\\u2022 Their total liability is capped at \\u201cthe fees paid or payable to Partner,\\u201d and they generally disclaim warranties for their site.\\nThis means:\\n\\u2022 Worst-case legal risks related to content, data, or IP are largely on you, while their downside is effectively limited to what they have already paid you.\\nPushback:\\n\\u2022 Add a reciprocal indemnity from them covering:\\n    \\u25e6 Their SDK, ad tech, tracking, and any UA / ad network practices on their side.\\n    \\u25e6 Infringement by their branding or assets, and violations of data protection laws arising from their processing.\\n\\u2022 Introduce caps and carve-outs:\\n    \\u25e6 Cap your indemnity and their liability at a defined multiple of annual fees, with higher caps only for IP or data breaches if needed.\\n\\u2022 Tighten the IP warranties so you are not giving absolute guarantees far beyond what is realistic.\\nG. Right of first refusal on variations (sequels etc.)\\nProblem:\\n\\u2022 The exclusivity clause says that where There is an exclusive game, Publisher has a right of first refusal on variations (sequels, prequels, etc.) under the same terms and conditions.\\nIn this specific Game Order the license is \\u201cnon-exclusive,\\u201d so this clause should not bite now, but it is still sitting There.\\nPushback:\\n\\u2022 Explicitly state in the main agreement or Game Order that:\\n    \\u25e6 \\u201cThe exclusivity provisions and right of first refusal in Annex 2, Article 8 do not apply to this Agreement or to any variations of the Games unless explicitly agreed in a future Game Order.\\u201d\\nThis prevents later arguments that you owe them first dibs on sequels.\\n\\nH. Self-billing, reporting, and audit\\nProblem:\\n\\u2022 They issue self-billing invoices and if you do not object within a short time window, they are deemed accepted.\\n\\u2022 Strong offset rights if ad networks fail to pay them.\\n\\u2022 No explicit reporting detail or audit rights are spelled out.\\nPushback:\\n\\u2022 Ask for:\\n    \\u25e6 Monthly detailed revenue reports by platform, geography, ad network, and ad/IAP split.\\n    \\u25e6 A clear dispute window of at least 30 days from receipt of a statement, with a defined process.\\n    \\u25e6 A right to audit or have a third-party auditor review their numbers once per year at your cost if discrepancies above a threshold are found.\\nI. Governing law and venue\\nProblem:\\n\\u2022 Belgium law, courts of Leuven for any disputes.\\nIf you can live with that, you leave it. If you want less friction:\\n\\u2022 Propose arbitration in a neutral venue or at least a less one-sided forum clause.\\n\\u2022 At minimum, you can leave this as \\u201cnot a hill to die on\\u201d if your main concern is web scope and lock-in, but be aware of the litigation friction.\\n3. Priority list given your goals\\nGiven what you said you care about (web only, shorter lockdown, easy exit, control if they disappoint), I would prioritize:\\n1. *Scope and platforms*: Remove \\u201cmobile app stores\\u201d from Licensed Platforms and make this a pure web publishing deal.\\n2. *Term and exit*: Add mutual termination for convenience with 30 days notice after an initial test period, and shorten or heavily constrain the 6-month Transition Period.\\n3. *Transferability / assignment*: Remove transferability beyond affiliates and require your consent for assignments.\\n4. *Monetization and links*: Explicit rights to link to and promote your own mobile versions and titles, within clear UX bounds.\\n5. *Indemnity balance*: Add mutual SDK / UA indemnity, cap your exposure, and fix the asymmetry.\\n6. *Support tail*: Limit SDK and support obligations after termination.\\nIf you paste your current redline or the email you are sending back, I can rewrite it to focus precisely on these points so There is no ambiguity.\", \"channel\": \"C07C2866011\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID\", \"thread_ts\": \"1763421013.739279\"}, {\"ts\": \"1764793154.009679\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"Short answer: for a venture-backed US studio like Harmony Games, you should assume *somewhere in the 20k\\u201380k USD range for legal + related professional fees*, with a realistic \\u201cplan for pain\\u201d budget around *50k*. Rough fee ranges by category\\nThese are order-of-magnitude numbers for a company like yours, using a mix of decent startup counsel + a scrappy accountant, not BigLaw overkill.\\nA. corporate dissolution & governance: *10k\\u201330k*\\nCovers things like:\\n\\u2022 Board and stockholder approvals.\\n\\u2022 Formal dissolution with Delaware, plus any foreign registrations (e.g. NC, CA, WA).\\n\\u2022 Handling investor rights, preference stack, and confirming There is no distribution or a small pro-rata distribution.\\n\\u2022 Drafting or reviewing:\\n    \\u25e6 Plan of liquidation / dissolution.\\n    \\u25e6 Officer certificates.\\n    \\u25e6 Releases and indemnities where needed.\\nIf everything is organized and you work with current counsel efficiently, you might land around *10k\\u201315k*. 1. What the contract actually does (plain summary)
*Parties and scope*
• Between MAXFLOW BV (CrazyGames) as Publisher and Harmony Games as Partner.
• Covers Domino Delights and Zombie Match 3D.
• License: world-wide, non-exclusive, _transferable_ license to publish the games on “Licensed Platforms.”
*Licensed Platforms*
Defined very broadly as:
• <http://CrazyGames.com|CrazyGames.com> and its domains / apps
• other WebGL or HTML5 browser platforms
• mobile app stores
So by default this contract covers both web and mobile, not just CrazyGames.
*Revenue share*
• Game Revenue is defined as ad + IAP revenue _after_ deducting: agency commissions, ad serving costs, platform fees, payment processing, and VAT/other taxes.
• Net amount is then split: 40 % Publisher, 60 % Partner.
*Hosting and SDK*
• Technology is “Publisher hosting” for these games, so you give them a full build, they host it.
• You must integrate their SDK, keep it up to date, and, on request, update SDK to the most recent version up to 1 year _after termination_ or make it possible for them to integrate the SDK into the game themselves.
*Game updates and parity*
You must:
• Deliver the game within 6 months.
• Keep the web version “always identical to the latest version” on your own sites and any other platforms.
• Ship updates to them no later than anyone else, fix bugs promptly, and provide reasonable ongoing support.
*Outbound links and monetization*
• You cannot include outbound links in the game (for example to your site or app stores) without their explicit written consent.
• They have the exclusive right to serve ads and IAPs on Licensed Platforms. You can only include IAPs with their approval.
*Term, renewal, and transition*
• Initial term: 1 year starting when the game is released on the Licensed Platforms.
• Automatic renewal for the same period, unless a party gives 3 months written notice before the end of a term.
• After expiry or termination, they _may_ keep the game live for a 6-month “Transition Period” and you must keep providing services and cooperation during that time.
*Termination*
• Both parties can terminate for material breach, insolvency, etc., with cure periods for some items.
• Publisher has extra rights to terminate immediately, without liability, if There is alleged IP infringement, breach of warranties, or breach of your obligations.
• There is _no_ mutual termination for convenience anywhere.
*Liability, indemnity, and IP*
• You give broad warranties that you own all IP, do not infringe, comply with laws, no viruses, high quality, etc.
• You indemnify them for IP infringements, legal breaches, and any claims about game content, with no explicit cap.
• Their liability is capped at “fees paid or payable to Partner under the Agreement” and they disclaim most warranties for their portal.
• They can act in your name to issue takedowns against copycats, but have no duty to litigate.
*Data and marketing*
• Each party is an independent controller for personal data, must comply with GDPR etc.
• You cannot use personal data beyond what is necessary, and cannot promote your own or third-party content on their platforms without their written consent.
*Law and venue*
• Governing law: Belgium.
• Exclusive courts: Leuven, Belgium.
2. Key red flags and items to Push on
A. Platform scope: they are grabbing mobile by default
Problem:
• Licensed Platforms includes “mobile app stores,” and the license is world-wide, transferable, and covers publishing and monetization There.
• Combined with their exclusive right to serve ads and IAP on Licensed Platforms, this pulls mobile into their control unless you carve it out.
Pushback / clarification:
• Restrict the Licensed Platforms to _web only_ for this agreement, for example:
    ◦ “Licensed Platforms: <http://www.CrazyGames.com|www.CrazyGames.com> and other HTML5/WebGL browser game portals. For the avoidance of doubt, this Agreement does not apply to any mobile app store distribution.”
• Or, if you want to allow some mobile experiment later, create a _separate_ mobile addendum with tight scope and your veto on any mobile publishing.
This aligns with your plan to keep mobile separate and talk to other mobile publishers.

B. Transferable license + easy assignment by them
Problem:
• License is explicitly “transferable.”
• Assignment clause lets _them_ assign the whole agreement to a third party with only notification, while you cannot assign without their consent.
This means they can sell or spin out your games’ web rights to another company without your approval.
Pushback:
• Make the license non-transferable except to their owned affiliates, or require your prior written consent for any assignment or sublicensing to non-affiliates.
• Make assignment more symmetric: you can at least assign to an acquirer of Harmony Games without needing their consent.
C. Term, auto-renewal, no convenience exit, plus 6-month transition
Problem:
• Initial 1-year term, automatic 1-year renewals, and you must give 3 months notice before the term ends to stop renewal.
• After any end, they can keep the game live for 6 more months, and you must support it.
• There is no termination for convenience for you at all.
In practice that is a long lockdown. If you miss the 3-month window, you are locked for another year plus up to 6 months of transition.
Pushback:
• Add mutual termination for convenience, for example:
    ◦ “After the first 3 months from launch, either Party may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon 30 days written notice.”
• Reduce the Transition Period or remove it. If you accept any transition, limit it to 30 days, and clarify that:
    ◦ Your support obligation is minimal (no new features, only critical bug fixes).
    ◦ They cannot launch the game on new platforms during the transition.
• If they insist on the 6-month Transition Period, tie it only to expiry of a term, not to early termination for convenience or breach.
This directly reduces the lockdown period you are worried about.

D. SDK and support obligations, including after termination
Problem:
• You must implement and keep their SDK up to date, and on request update it “until 1 year after termination,” or else “make it possible for Publisher to integrate the SDK within the Game(s) itself.”
• You must keep the web version identical to the latest version on all other platforms, deliver updates to them no later than others, quickly fix defects, and answer their questions.
Risks:
• You are on the hook for live-ops style support even when the deal is effectively over.
• “Make it possible for Publisher to integrate the SDK” is vague and could be interpreted as pressure to expose more of your build pipeline or code than you want.
Pushback:
• Limit post-termination obligations: for example, “up to 60 days after termination, best-effort support limited to critical bug fixes, no new SDK integrations.”
• Clarify that you are not required to provide source code or build scripts and that SDK integration will always be done by you at your discretion.
• Relax “always identical” wording so you can test features on other platforms first or maintain a lighter web build.
E. Monetization and outbound links: they control everything
Problem:
• They have the exclusive right to serve ads and IAPs within the game on Licensed Platforms.
• You cannot add Outbound Links or promote your own or third-party content through their platforms without explicit written consent.
Impact:
• You cannot naturally promote your own mobile versions or cross-promote your other games from the web build without their explicit permission.
• Any IAP system in the web version requires their approval and flows through their billing.
Pushback:
• Carve out specific outbound links that are always allowed, for example:
    ◦ “Partner may include links to Partner’s official website, and to Domino Delights and Zombie Match mobile store pages, subject to Publisher’s UX requirements, without separate written approval.”
• Clarify that cross-promotion of your own titles within the game is permitted, provided it does not conflict with their ad inventory.
• If you ever want to test your own IAP stack on web, you need at least a negotiation clause instead of pure veto.
F. Indemnities and liability are very one-sided
Problem:
• Your indemnity is broad and uncapped in the text: IP infringement, data protection, any claims about content, plus breach of warranties.
• Their total liability is capped at “the fees paid or payable to Partner,” and they generally disclaim warranties for their site.
This means:
• Worst-case legal risks related to content, data, or IP are largely on you, while their downside is effectively limited to what they have already paid you.
Pushback:
• Add a reciprocal indemnity from them covering:
    ◦ Their SDK, ad tech, tracking, and any UA / ad network practices on their side.
    ◦ Infringement by their branding or assets, and violations of data protection laws arising from their processing.
• Introduce caps and carve-outs:
    ◦ Cap your indemnity and their liability at a defined multiple of annual fees, with higher caps only for IP or data breaches if needed.
• Tighten the IP warranties so you are not giving absolute guarantees far beyond what is realistic.
G. Right of first refusal on variations (sequels etc.)

Reconciled every sub-ticket against merged PRs in `harmonygames-Games/GameOfDominoes`. Source of truth = merged code, not the review column.

**Confirmed shipped → flipped to Done** (code was merged months ago but tickets were stuck in PR/Validation):
- ENG-2417 Settings (PR #1901), ENG-2418 Level-win (#1902), ENG-2419 Level Lose/Out-of-moves (#1903), ENG-2425 Nathan's Treasure (#1895), ENG-2426 Axe Arena (#1908)

- ENG-2410 Shop, ENG-2414 Leaderboard, ENG-2415 Quest, ENG-2424 Collect&win (Magical Wings), ENG-2427 River Rush, ENG-2428 Season Pass, ENG-2429 Remove Ad, ENG-2430 Offers, ENG-2431 Rate-us Pop-ups, ENG-2437 Daily Gift

Net: 10 tickets flipped to Done, 10 confirmed unstarted. Core-Game epic (ENG-2403) still has Shop/Leaderboard/Quest outstanding; Live-Ops epic (ENG-2404) still has Collect&win/River Rush/Season Pass/Remove Ad/Offers/Rate-us/Daily Gift outstanding.

input.title: Move off Helpshift — DD & Zombie Match (winddown)
input.description:
Tracking ticket created during the 2026-02-28 winddown cleanup so the Helpshift decommission is captured in Linear instead of living only in chat/subscriptions.

## Context
- Helpshift is our in-app customer-support SDK in **both** live games: Domino Delights (repo `GameOfDominoes`) and Zombie Match 3D (repo `match3d`).
- As part of the shutdown, the **Helpshift subscription is being cancelled** — 2026-02-28 is the cutoff for both games. Outstanding invoices were paid off (Feb 10). After cutoff, anything routing to the Helpshift service stops working.

## Where it stands (as of 2026-02-28)
**Already shipped — self-serve fallback so players aren't stranded when Helpshift dies:**
- DD: ENG-2399 "Contact Us button + user ID on splash screen and error pop-up" — **Done** (merged, Nov 2025).
- ZM: ZOM-594 "Contact Us button in splash screen" — **Done** (Oct 2025); ZOM-314 settings panel with Contact Us + Copy ID — **Done**.

**Not done / open:**
- The **Helpshift SDK is still bundled** in both shipped apps, and the in-app/settings "Contact Us" still opens a Helpshift conversation → this path breaks once the subscription lapses.
- No merged PR removes/disables Helpshift in either repo (searched both — only the original integrations exist).
- No new store builds are planned during winddown, so a full SDK-strip + resubmit is not realistic.

## Remaining work / decision needed
- [ ] Confirm final disposition with founders: **accept graceful degradation** (Helpshift chat goes dead; the shipped self-serve Contact Us + Copy-User-ID email path remains the support channel) vs. shipping builds that remove/disable the Helpshift Contact Us. Given winddown + no planned releases, graceful degradation is the likely call.
- [ ] Cancel/close the Helpshift account (ops — tracked on the winddown subscription list; appears handled).
- [ ] (If desired) repoint the in-app "Contact Us" to a static support email so the button doesn't dead-end after cutoff.

— Arthur Blake, winddown tracker cleanup

Rundown as promised — tracker is cleaned up and reflects reality now, so Leonard & Robert aren't guessing. (Sorry for the delay, I was heads-down on the Unity upgrade build all week.)

*1) Tracker cleanup (Linear) — done*
• *Telegram:* the whole Telegram/DD push was called off in January (Leonard terminated [PERSON_NAME_0133]'s contract Jan 6, "we changed directions, not doing telegram anytime soon"). I canceled the master ticket (ENG-2377) + all 6 open sub-tickets and left a note on the master pointing at that decision. The 2 sub-tasks that were genuinely finished before the pivot stay Done. So the export no longer says we're actively building a Telegram game.
• *UI Optimization sprint:* reconciled every ticket against merged PRs (not the review column).
    ◦ 10 were actually merged months ago but stuck in PR/Validation → flipped to Done (Settings, Level-win, Level-lose, Nathan's Treasure, Axe Arena, + all 4 mini-games and their parent).
    ◦ 10 had *no code behind them* at all → moved out of review to Todo with an audit note on each: Shop, Leaderboard, Quest, Collect&win, River Rush, Season Pass, Remove Ad, Offers, Rate-us, Daily Gift. Full audit is on the UI master (ENG-2401).

*2) Helpshift move vs today's cutoff*
Net: *not fully off it, but players won't be stranded.* The self-serve fallback already shipped in both games — Contact Us + Copy-User-ID on the splash/error screens (DD ENG-2399, ZM ZOM-594/314, all Done). BUT the Helpshift SDK is still bundled in both live apps and the in-settings "Contact Us" still opens a Helpshift chat, which goes dead when the subscription lapses today. No removal code was ever written and no new store builds are planned. I created *ENG-2438* to track it — realistic call given winddown is to accept graceful degradation (chat dies, email/ID fallback remains) rather than ship SDK-strip builds. Flagging so you can confirm that's fine.

*3) What Sunset is still waiting on*
• Linear + Trello exports into their shared drive — after today's cleanup the tracker is accurate and ready to export; the actual drop is the last step on my side.
• Leonard still owes their tech guy the answer on whether exporting our private Slack channels needs the Business+ upgrade (that one's on you).

*4) CrazyGames deal*
Publishing agreement was *signed early December* (web-only, CrazyGames.com; covers Domino Delights + Zombie Match 3D; 60/40 rev share in our favor). *Integration was never started* — it needs the CrazyGames SDK added + the economy rework to remove hearts/lives, none of which happened. Their PM is still pinging Robert about the web version. With the shutdown this won't be built; heads-up that the contract had a ~6-month delivery obligation, so it should go on the list of deals to formally wind down with the other vendor terminations.

*5) Other genuinely-open engineering items*
• Helpshift decommission (ENG-2438) — above.
• CrazyGames integration — never started (above); dead in winddown.
• UI-opt: the 10 no-code screens above are unbuilt but moot now.
• Unity upgrade build — what I was on this week; likely moot given we're terminating the Unity Pro license.
• Data-tail systems (GitHub, Metabase/dbt, Slack, Google) staying up until data is extracted/sold, per the subscription plan.

That's the full picture — tracker is honest now and safe to hand over.
